statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at the low edge of the watch band as the overnight path retraces in both directions, while Stress stays high on a 5.24% 10-year yield and crude near $93.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases. Outside that window the published forecast returns to the watch and low bands.
headline: Overnight NQ recovers its early-session dip while the 10-year yield stalls at 5.24% below Monday's two-decade high
body: NQ front-month trades near 30,591, up 0.08% on the session, after an overnight range of 30,372.25-30,626.00. That path is two-way rather than directional: index futures were quoted roughly 0.44% lower around 05:54 UTC and have since fully retraced the decline, which is the central reason Tail stays at the low edge of the watch band. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, but finished about 200 points above its 30,081.06 session low, and ES futures are effectively unchanged at 7,745.00. The macro backdrop remains genuinely difficult. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.24%, its highest since 2007, with the 30-year near 5.56%, and roughly 70% odds of an October Federal Reserve rate increase are priced. WTI crude is near $93.24, up 0.69%, having faded from an overnight high of $94.74 after Iran's foreign minister left New York without an extended Strait of Hormuz agreement. Against that, VIX is subdued at 16.17 inside a narrow 15.98-16.19 range and the 10-year is close to unchanged on the day, so the two amplifiers that drove Monday's decline are pausing rather than extending. Latest-session shared context shows a heavy but dispersed technology tape: seven of eight megacaps lower with META down 4.79% and TSLA down 3.94%, and the tracked semiconductor basket averaging -3.86% with ARM down 8.70%, QCOM down 7.17% and INTC down 5.67%, while NVDA rose against the complex after announcing a $150 billion buyback. That dispersion argues for high Stress rather than a lethal one-way path. The flagged window covers the 13:30 UTC cash open through the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence stack. Those releases have not printed at the time of this assessment, so no post-event continuation is treated as observed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours were published. Tail ranged from 17 to 27, with only two single-hour excursions into the elevated band, at 09:00 and 14:00 UTC on Monday, each reverting within the following hour. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, then oscillated between 20 and 24 from 01:00 UTC as the European handover approached, printing 20 in each of the last two hours. Stress never fell below 76 and peaked at 85 at 10:00 UTC on Monday, reflecting the persistent high-yield and high-oil regime rather than any single release. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail in the watch band through the European and early US session, with a single elevated-band hour at 14:00 UTC where JOLTS Job Openings, JOLTS Job Quits and CB Consumer Confidence print 30 minutes into the US cash session. That stacking of the opening auction with high-impact releases is the only flagged hour, and Tail is modelled to decay back into the watch band by 15:00 UTC on an orderly price-discovery assumption. Overnight hours into Wednesday return to the low band before Tail steps back to the watch band from 05:00 UTC, as the European handover approaches the 12:15 UTC ADP release and the 12:30 UTC core PCE and final Q2 GDP block that falls outside this 24-hour window.

Retracements are working, so Tail stays at the low edge of the watch band despite Monday's 1.08% cash decline.
